_comment: Pathological client scenarios that stress-test agent assumptions. Each scenario targets a different edge case in the CMMC consulting methodology.

scenarios.name: OceanTech Instruments (University Spinout)
edge_cases: Shared lab with Navy — personnel overlap creates CUI determination ambiguity
Grant vs contract instrument type — DFARS may not apply to grants
PI has dual appointments (university + company)
Lab equipment is government-furnished (GFE) via cooperative agreement
Students access CUI systems as part of research — personnel screening gap

org_profile.name: OceanTech Instruments LLC
org_profile.parent_relationship: Spinout from URI, shared lab space

current_contracts._comment: Grants may not include DFARS 7012 — agent should flag this

intake_answers.system_boundary: Shared URI lab, 3 dedicated workstations, URI network segment, personal laptops used for email
intake_answers.it_staff: None dedicated — PI configures systems, URI IT provides network
intake_answers.cui_flow: CUI generated in lab (sensor data), stored on local NAS, shared via email with Navy PM
intake_answers.email_provider: URI institutional email (Google Workspace for Education)
intake_answers.endpoint_protection: URI-managed Sophos on shared lab machines, nothing on personal laptops
intake_answers.mfa: URI SSO with Duo MFA for lab machines, no MFA on NAS
intake_answers.backup: Manual USB backup to PI's home, no offsite
intake_answers.incident_response: Would call URI IT — no formal IR plan
intake_answers.physical_security: URI campus card access to building, lab locked with key
intake_answers.media_protection: USB drives in PI's desk drawer, not encrypted
intake_answers.personnel: 3 employees + 2 URI grad students + PI with dual appointment
intake_answers.gfe: 2 hydrophones and 1 signal processor on loan from NAVSEA

expected_agent_flags: Grant instrument may not require CMMC — verify DFARS clause presence
Shared URI network creates system boundary ambiguity
Personal laptops in scope if used for CUI-adjacent work
GFE handling requires specific controls (MP family)
Grad students need CUI access agreements and screening
USB backup to PI's home is a CUI spillage risk
Google Workspace for Education may not meet FedRAMP Moderate

scenarios.name: Precision Coatings (3-Person Company)
edge_cases: Owner wears all hats — IT admin, CISO, compliance officer, machinist
No IT staff — consumer-grade everything
Budget under $5K/year for all IT
Realistic: M365 Business Basic, consumer Netgear router, Ring camera
Every answer is 'Jane does it'

intake_answers.system_boundary: One desktop in shop office, one laptop (Jane's), shop floor PC for CNC machine
intake_answers.cui_flow: Receives specs via email (PDF), stores on desktop, prints for shop floor
intake_answers.mfa: None — 'too complicated, it's just me and two guys'
intake_answers.physical_security: Deadbolt on shop door, no alarm, Ring doorbell camera
intake_answers.media_protection: Specs printed and filed in shop cabinet

expected_agent_flags: M365 Business Basic may not include required compliance features — need Business Premium or E3+
Consumer router has no FIPS-validated encryption, no VLAN capability
No MFA is a critical gap for AC and IA families
No backup = no MP.L2-3.8.9 compliance
CNC machine PC in scope if connected to network with CUI
Recommendations must be realistic for $5K budget
Do NOT recommend SIEM, SOC, or enterprise tools for 3 people
Ring camera is consumer IoT — physical security gap

scenarios.name: Meridian Analytics (Cloud-Only)
edge_cases: No on-prem infrastructure — entire system boundary is cloud
Multiple SaaS providers create complex shared responsibility
GFE handled by prime contractor (Meridian is sub)
Remote-only workforce — no office
AWS GovCloud + commercial SaaS mix

intake_answers.system_boundary: AWS GovCloud (analytics platform), Microsoft 365 E5 (email/collab), Salesforce (CRM, no CUI), Okta (SSO/MFA)
intake_answers.it_staff: 1 DevOps engineer, uses Okta admin + AWS admin
intake_answers.cui_flow: Receives CUI datasets from NG via SFTP to S3, processes in EC2, results delivered via encrypted SharePoint
intake_answers.endpoint_protection: CrowdStrike Falcon on all company laptops (managed via Intune)
intake_answers.mfa: Okta Verify (push) for all apps, hardware keys for AWS admin
intake_answers.backup: AWS S3 versioning + cross-region replication, M365 retention policies
intake_answers.incident_response: Written IR plan, NG CIRT notified per subcontract, CrowdStrike managed detection
intake_answers.physical_security: No office — all remote. Company laptops shipped with Bitlocker enabled.
intake_answers.media_protection: No removable media policy — USB ports disabled via Intune
intake_answers.personnel: 12 employees, all cleared Secret, annual security awareness via KnowBe4
intake_answers.gfe: None — all equipment company-furnished. NG provides SFTP credentials only

expected_agent_flags: System boundary is 100% cloud — PE controls may be inherited from CSPs
Shared responsibility model: AWS GovCloud (FedRAMP High) vs M365 (FedRAMP Moderate)
Salesforce must be explicitly OUT of scope if no CUI touches it
Subcontract flow-down — CMMC requirement comes from NG, not direct DoD
Remote workforce means PE controls are home-office focused
SFTP credential management is a critical IA control
Strong existing posture — likely close to compliant already

scenarios.name: Hawkeye Defense Systems (ITAR + CUI Mixed)
edge_cases: Dual CUI markings: CUI Basic and CUI Specified (ITAR)
ITAR overlay requires additional controls beyond CMMC L2
Export control adds personnel citizenship requirements
Different handling requirements for different data types
Foreign national employees create ITAR complications

intake_answers.system_boundary: On-prem AD domain, Palo Alto firewall, VMware cluster, classified//unclassified air-gapped lab, 3 remote engineers via VPN
intake_answers.it_staff: IT Director + 2 sysadmins, dedicated InfoSec analyst
intake_answers.cui_flow: ITAR data in air-gapped lab only, CUI Basic on main network, engineering drawings cross boundary via sneakernet (approved USB)
intake_answers.endpoint_protection: Symantec Endpoint on all domain machines, CrowdStrike on air-gapped lab (standalone)
intake_answers.mfa: RSA SecurID for VPN and admin, smart cards for ITAR lab access
intake_answers.backup: Veeam to on-prem NAS (encrypted), ITAR systems backed up to separate encrypted NAS in vault
intake_answers.incident_response: Formal IR plan, DCSA reported per DFARS 7012, DDTC notified for ITAR incidents
intake_answers.physical_security: Alarmed facility, mantrap for ITAR lab, CCTV, visitor logs, all doors badge-access
intake_answers.media_protection: ITAR media in GSA-approved safe, CUI media in locked cabinet, degaussing for disposal
intake_answers.personnel: 38 US citizens, 4 permanent residents (no ITAR access), 3 foreign nationals (ITAR-restricted areas physically separated)
intake_answers.gfe: 2 classified laptops (stored in SCIF), 1 test fixture from PEO Missiles

expected_agent_flags: ITAR data requires DDTC notification for incidents — separate from DFARS 7012
Air-gapped lab is a separate security domain — may need its own SSP section
Sneakernet USB transfers between domains need strict media protection controls
Foreign national employees must be physically separated from ITAR-controlled areas
Permanent residents may access CUI Basic but NOT ITAR technical data
Two different CUI handling procedures needed: CUI Basic vs CUI//ITAR
Existing security posture is mature — focus on documentation, not remediation
GFE classified laptops in SCIF are likely out of CMMC scope
